is for the surfaces that administer the ``parent_customer`` hierarchy rather
than choose a payer.

post.summary: Generate and download a daily report PDF
post.description:
Generate and download a daily report for a service order line.

Access is scoped to the authenticated user's customer projects.
If date is omitted, the report covers all activity dates for the SOL.

``require_content=False`` — the deliberate opt-out from the empty-day refusal
the internal surfaces take. ``date`` may be omitted here, so "empty" means
"this line has no activity at all", not "nothing happened that day"; the
caller is a portal in another repository whose 4xx handling we cannot see;
and there is no dialog here to show a message in. A customer asking for a
quiet line gets the quiet PDF rather than an error.

post.summary: Download a final (SOL) report — engine-rendered or uploaded
post.description:
Download the final report for a service order line, whatever its type.

The single final-report entry point for the portal — callers do not need to
know how a given service's report is produced. Services outside
``_UPLOADED_FINAL_REPORT_PREFIXES`` are rendered by the engine on demand; the
rest have no engine template, so the document ops uploaded is streamed from
storage the way ``core.endpoints.files`` serves stored files (GCS blob bytes
with the blob's own content type, falling back to a public-URL redirect).
Either way the response is the file bytes with a download
``Content-Disposition``, so the client handles one shape. A response is not
necessarily a PDF: an uploaded LER report may be a DOCX/XLSX/ZIP, and its
``Content-Type`` says so.

The customer-facing counterpart of the technician ``final-report/download``
endpoint (AECP-303): access is scoped to the caller's customer purely by
PostgreSQL RLS on ``ServiceOrderLine`` (via ``ServiceOrderHeader.customer_id``)
— a SOL the caller cannot see is not found, and that gate stays ahead of
*both* branches. LPS SOLs resolve the project's ``lps_standard_id`` for the
engine; a missing template is a clear 4xx, as is an LER SOL whose report has
not been uploaded yet (404).

get.summary: Download an uploaded final report file (e.g. LER)
get.description:
Download the uploaded final report attached to a service order line.

Deprecated in favour of ``POST /final``, which now serves uploaded finals
itself, so no client needs to classify the report type. Kept — and marked
deprecated in the schema rather than described as such in prose — for clients
pinned to the two-endpoint contract; it delegates to the same resolution
helpers, so the two cannot drift.

The customer-safe uploaded-file path (TD-1 / AECP-267). Ownership is
**verified, not assumed**: the SOL is resolved through the RLS-scoped
queryset first, so a SOL outside the caller's customer is invisible → 404,
and only then is its linked file served. This deliberately does **not** proxy
the generic ``/api/core/v1/files/service_order_line/{id}/`` endpoint, which
carries no customer RLS and no report permission.

post.summary: Request a custom report for a selection of turbines, locations or projects
post.description:
Start rendering one document for the selection; returns a generation id to poll.

The selection is resolved and refused here, before the engine is called: an id
outside the caller's customer, an unknown ``report_type``, band value or anomaly
type, an empty result and an oversized selection are each a 422 naming the cause.
Requesting needs the Reports feature's Full level (``CUSTOMER_MANAGE_REPORTS``);
following the request needs View.

get.summary: List the customer's latest custom report requests
get.description: The caller's newest requests first, each with its family, status and the selection it was made for, so a finished document can be offered without a new render.

get.summary: List the report types a custom report can be requested for
get.description: The registered families with the request fields each reads and its selection cap, so the portal form is driven by the server.
Poll a pending request once; it turns complete only after the PDF is stored in Ops Hub's own file store.
Serve the stored PDF of a completed request under the name it was stored with; the engine is never called.

when available, then falls back to auto-discovery if it is missing or invalid.

Manually transition a project from Closure to Completed.

The cascade only advances projects up to Closure (all SOLs Completed or
Cancelled). Moving to Completed is an explicit close-out action — there
is no automatic trigger.

Manually set a project's status, bypassing the stage gates.

Privileged override gated behind the ``force_complete_project`` permission.
Any status except Cancelled can be set, in either direction, including
reopening a Completed project. Rules, audit trail, and the deliberate
no-side-effects contract live in ``ProjectManager.override_status``. The
automatic status rules (SOL cascade, nightly reconciler) stay active and
may later move the status again.

put.description:
Set or clear the customer pre-job questionnaire 'received' timestamp.

This is the Core replacement for the legacy ``PUT /projects/{id}/user-status``
pre-job workflow path. Only the *null-ness* of ``payload.pre_job_received_at``
is read — it signals intent; the timestamp itself is stamped **server-side**
(``timezone.now()``) to stay robust against client clock skew:

- ``null -> non-null`` (customer **submit**): stamps the timestamp, sends the
  pre-job submission notification, and re-runs the Pipedrive status cascade
  (advancing the project to Planning when probability is 100).
- ``non-null -> null`` (staff **reopen**): clears the timestamp; no email,
  no cascade.
- already-received re-submit: keeps the existing timestamp; no side effects.

Return all data needed for the dispatching board.

Aggregates:
- Project resource sets with their members
- All project workorders (service + admin) with resource assignments
- Service order lines grouped for the panel

When both ``since`` and ``until`` are supplied, the workorders list is
filtered to a date window — useful for the dispatching console where
only the relevant working set should be returned. The five filter
clauses are: scheduled in window, mandatory in window,
assigned-but-unscheduled, due-dated backlog within
``dispatch.managers.board_reads.BACKLOG_HORIZON_DAYS``, and unassigned
WOs from PLANNING/EXECUTION projects (regardless of due date). Without
the params, the legacy behaviour is preserved (returns all non-cancelled
workorders).

The windowed result also folds in real work that was logged but never
formally dispatched (DISP-4368, see
``dispatch.managers.logged_unplanned._get_logged_unplanned_workorders``)
-- those rows carry ``is_logged_unplanned=True`` with a planned window
derived from the actual logged activity times, and are dropped entirely
if that derived window clashes with a genuinely planned entry for one of
the same resources.

``dispatch.managers.board_reads._get_project_turbines``).

get.summary: Server-filtered, paginated work-order list for the dispatch sidebar
get.description:
Sidebar work-order list with server-side filtering and pagination.

A large project can hold thousands of unassigned workorders — shipping
them all inside ``board-data`` made the board slow and the browser
unstable, so the sidebar reads this endpoint instead (and ``board-data``
is called with ``include_backlog=false``).

Filters: ``q`` full-text-ish search (name, description, service code,
turbine name, SO number); ``assignment`` open|unassigned|assigned, where
``assigned`` means an active resource-set link EXISTS, ``unassigned`` means
none does, and ``open`` (the default, what the sidebar shows) is
unassigned work PLUS any ``IN_PROGRESS`` workorder regardless of its team
link -- running work that was dispatched earlier still has to be found
and moved to the next day when it does not finish, and it normally still
carries its team; ``statuses``/``kinds``/``service_codes`` as
comma-separated lists; ``logged_unplanned`` narrows to (``true``) or
excludes (``false``) real work logged with no formal dispatch (DISP-4368)
-- these rows are already part of the unassigned scope and otherwise
indistinguishable by status from any untouched backlog WO, so this is
what makes them findable across a project's full backlog rather than only
on whichever board day/week they happen to be scrolled to. ``counts`` in
the response carries facet totals for the filter chips, each computed
before its own facet filter (standard faceting), over the search +
assignment scope.

See ``dispatch.managers.backlog._get_backlog_sync`` for the query shape:
the assignment counts come from one query (grouping on a ``has_team``
annotation rather than filtering `base` twice), and the three facet
breakdowns (statuses/kinds/services) come from one grouped query across
all three dimensions at once, summed per dimension in Python.

Hourly weather forecast for a project location on ``date``.

The whole UTC day, read from the ``weather_forecast`` cache (kept warm by the scheduled Gust sync). On a
cache miss for an in-horizon day, the location's bucket is backfilled from
Gust on the fly (one query) and re-read. Fail-soft: returns
``available=false`` with no hours when the location has no coordinates or no
forecast is available, so the board always renders.

For each project active in the window, return the total active resource
sets and the per-day count of resource sets with at least one workorder
planned to start on that day. Coverage % is computed client-side.

The workorder is scoped to ``project_id`` and inherits the project's

member's person lane.

The manager creates, links, and pins the workorder inside one
transaction: if the resource-set or assignee step fails, the workorder
must not be left committed without its dispatch links (mirrors the

get.description:
Return all readiness rows; optionally filter by project status code.

When omitted, no status filter is applied. ``include_null_status`` keeps

Return all data needed for the dispatching board.

Aggregates:
- Project resource sets with their members
- All project workorders (service + admin) with resource assignments
- Service order lines grouped for the panel

When both ``since`` and ``until`` are supplied, the workorders list is
filtered to a date window — useful for the dispatching console where
only the relevant working set should be returned. The five filter
clauses are: scheduled in window, mandatory in window,
assigned-but-unscheduled, due-dated backlog within
``dispatch.managers.board_reads.BACKLOG_HORIZON_DAYS``, and unassigned
WOs from PLANNING/EXECUTION projects (regardless of due date). Without
the params, the legacy behaviour is preserved (returns all non-cancelled
workorders).

The windowed result also folds in real work that was logged but never
formally dispatched (DISP-4368, see
``dispatch.managers.logged_unplanned._get_logged_unplanned_workorders``)
-- those rows carry ``is_logged_unplanned=True`` with a planned window
derived from the actual logged activity times, and are dropped entirely
if that derived window clashes with a genuinely planned entry for one of
the same resources.

get.summary: Get per-turbine status rollup for the dispatching board
get.description:
Per-turbine status + activity-group completion for the whole project,
regardless of the board's date window (see
``dispatch.managers.board_reads._get_project_turbines``).

Kept on its own query, decoupled from ``board-data``'s per-mutation
refetch cycle, since this scan covers every non-cancelled workorder in
the project and dominates payload size.

get.summary: Server-filtered, paginated work-order list for the dispatch sidebar
get.description:
Sidebar work-order list with server-side filtering and pagination.

A large project can hold thousands of unassigned workorders — shipping
them all inside ``board-data`` made the board slow and the browser
unstable, so the sidebar reads this endpoint instead (and ``board-data``
is called with ``include_backlog=false``).

Filters: ``q`` full-text-ish search (name, description, service code,
turbine name, SO number); ``assignment`` open|unassigned|assigned, where
``assigned`` means an active resource-set link EXISTS, ``unassigned`` means
none does, and ``open`` (the default, what the sidebar shows) is
unassigned work PLUS any ``IN_PROGRESS`` workorder regardless of its team
link -- running work that was dispatched earlier still has to be found
and moved to the next day when it does not finish, and it normally still
carries its team; ``statuses``/``kinds``/``service_codes`` as
comma-separated lists; ``logged_unplanned`` narrows to (``true``) or
excludes (``false``) real work logged with no formal dispatch (DISP-4368)
-- these rows are already part of the unassigned scope and otherwise
indistinguishable by status from any untouched backlog WO, so this is
what makes them findable across a project's full backlog rather than only
on whichever board day/week they happen to be scrolled to. ``counts`` in
the response carries facet totals for the filter chips, each computed
before its own facet filter (standard faceting), over the search +
assignment scope.

See ``dispatch.managers.backlog._get_backlog_sync`` for the query shape:
the assignment counts come from one query (grouping on a ``has_team``
annotation rather than filtering `base` twice), and the three facet
breakdowns (statuses/kinds/services) come from one grouped query across
all three dimensions at once, summed per dimension in Python.

Hourly weather forecast for a project location on ``date``.

The whole UTC day, read from the ``weather_forecast`` cache (kept warm by the scheduled Gust sync). On a
cache miss for an in-horizon day, the location's bucket is backfilled from
Gust on the fly (one query) and re-read. Fail-soft: returns
``available=false`` with no hours when the location has no coordinates or no
forecast is available, so the board always renders.

For each project active in the window, return the total active resource
sets and the per-day count of resource sets with at least one workorder
planned to start on that day. Coverage % is computed client-side.

post.summary: Create an ADMIN workorder assigned to a single technician
post.description:
Create a standalone ADMIN workorder pinned to one individual technician.

The workorder is scoped to ``project_id`` and inherits the project's
``requesting_customer`` (so it is visible under the customer-scoped RLS
policy and returned by ``board-data``). It is created with
``type=ADMIN`` / ``status=NOT_STARTED`` via the canonical
``WorkorderManager.gql_create`` path, then linked to the project resource
set the technician belongs to and pinned to that individual — reusing the
same assignment machinery as ``/assign`` so the board routes it into the
member's person lane.

The manager creates, links, and pins the workorder inside one
transaction: if the resource-set or assignee step fails, the workorder
must not be left committed without its dispatch links (mirrors the
atomic pattern in ``_assign_workorders_bulk_sync``).

- Cache: Local database table (fast, updated hourly)

    params: Query parameters including pagination, search, filters.

- page: Page number (default 1).

post.summary: Complete Work Orders (and cascade linked anomalies)
post.description:
Atomically complete each work order and advance its linked anomaly.

Productionises AECP-333 (pairs the portal's AECP-329 two-call orchestration):
per work order, in one transaction, set ``status=completed`` (stamping
``completed_date``) and — if it has a linked anomaly — advance that anomaly's
``stage`` -> ``RESOLUTION_COMPLETE`` (which recomputes ``resolution_status``
-> ``RESOLVED``). A WO with no anomaly completes with ``cascade="none"``; if a
WO's cascade fails, that WO rolls back (``cascade="failed"``) while the others
still succeed. Gated on work-management-manage; the cascade is RLS-scoped, so
it can only advance anomalies the caller's customer owns.

CustomerType.description:
What kind of party a customer row represents.

``COMMERCIAL`` is an ordinary customer: billable, mirrored to NetSuite, and the
answer every customer picker in the product is asking for.

``VIRTUAL`` is an organisation that exists only so a group of users can read
across the customers beneath it in the ``parent_customer`` tree. It is never
billed and never mirrored to NetSuite or Pipedrive.

The vocabulary lives here rather than in a database constraint, so adding a kind

ReceptorItem.description:
One receptor row in a sync (PUT) body for a single blade.

A receptor is a ``TurbineComponent`` with ``component_type`` Receptor or
HV Receptor and ``parent_turbine_component`` set to the owning blade.
The sync endpoint operates on the receptor children of one blade at a
time.

Upsert by ``id``: rows with ``id`` set update the matching record; rows
without ``id`` create a new one. Existing rows whose ``id`` is omitted
from the list are soft-deleted (full-list sync semantics).

ProjectScopeChangeRequestCustomFieldsOut.description:
Read-side twin of the custom-fields schema — must never 500 a GET.

``custom_fields`` has no DB type constraint, so a legacy or
hand-written row can violate the input contract the strict parent
enforces on create. On serialization, malformed ids degrade to null
(mirroring the regex-guarded SQL annotations that resolve the same
keys), unknown keys are surfaced as-is instead of failing the
response model, and the condition sections loosen to bare dicts —
the strict nested schemas would fail a GET over a hand-written row,
and the UI parses the sections defensively anyway.

source_service_order_line_id.description: Source SOL id. Required when the scope change is a service replacement; must be paired with replacement_service_id.
source_service_order_line_id.title: Source Service Order Line Id

source_turbine_component_id.description: TurbineComponent (blade) id the change applies to. Only meaningful on a service replacement whose source SOL covers the whole turbine (no pinned component): only the chosen blade's workorders move to the new SOL, and the source SOL stays active for the other blades. Omit (or null) to change the whole turbine — the source SOL is cancelled as before. On a blade-pinned source SOL the field must be absent or equal the pinned component.
source_turbine_component_id.title: Source Turbine Component Id

replacement_service_id.description: Replacement service id. Required when the scope change is a service replacement; must be paired with source_service_order_line_id.
replacement_service_id.title: Replacement Service Id

evidence_file_ids.description: core.File ids of evidence files previously uploaded via POST /api/core/v1/files. The backend creates a FileEntityLink row per id in the same transaction as the SCR; unknown ids cause the whole create to roll back with 422. The ids also persist in this JSON column as the historical input contract.
evidence_file_ids.title: Evidence File Ids

additional_workorders.description: Persisted copy of the top-level create field of the same name. The backend writes it here so a request that awaits QC → Sales → PM review still knows which workorders to generate when the finalize cascade eventually runs (possibly days after creation). Read-only in practice — supply the top-level create field instead of writing this key directly.
additional_workorders.title: Additional Workorders

ProjectScopeChangeRequestCreate.description:
Schema for creating a project scope change.

The service-replacement linkage (``source_service_order_line_id`` and
``replacement_service_id``) and evidence file references
(``evidence_file_ids``) live inside ``custom_fields`` — the payload
mirrors DB structure rather than inventing top-level body keys for
fields that don't have dedicated columns. ``additional_workorders``
is a sibling top-level body property (the historical wire contract);
the backend persists it into ``custom_fields`` so a request awaiting
review still honors it at the deferred finalize.

custom_fields.description: Scope-change metadata — service-replacement linkage and evidence file references. See ProjectScopeChangeRequestCustomFields.

additional_workorders.description: Optional follow-up generation step — service items from the replacement service to generate as NOT_STARTED workorders on the new SOL, each optionally narrowed to a subset of the source turbine's components. Strongly recommended; without this, the new SOL may end up at FIELD_COMPLETED right after the scope change because every migrated workorder is force-completed and no replacement-service work exists yet. Service item ids are validated at create time (must exist, be live, and belong to custom_fields.replacement_service_id — 422 otherwise). Persisted into custom_fields so a request awaiting review still honors it when the finalize cascade eventually runs.

initiated_from.description: Origin client. AeroTask must send AEROTASK — evidence images are mandatory for AeroTask-initiated requests (422 without at least one custom_fields.evidence_file_ids entry). Defaults to OPSHUB, for which evidence stays optional.

ProjectScopeChangeRequestUpdate.description:
Fields editable on a request that still awaits its first (QC) review.

The endpoint 422s on any other status — later review stages, APPROVED
(the cascade ran) and REJECTED (terminal) are immutable; correcting
those means reject + recreate. The source SOL and type are deliberately
not editable: re-pointing the request at a different line is a new
request. ``replacement_service_id`` and ``additional_workorders`` live
in ``custom_fields`` on the row; they are top-level here so the
editable surface stays an explicit whitelist.

replacement_service_id.description: New replacement service (stored as custom_fields.replacement_service_id). Must be an LER service. When it changes, additional_workorders must be re-submitted in the same call — the previously selected service items belong to the old replacement service.
replacement_service_id.title: Replacement Service Id

additional_workorders.description: Replaces the persisted additional_workorders plan; validated against the (possibly new) replacement service. Pass an empty list to clear the plan.
additional_workorders.title: Additional Workorders

evidence_file_ids.description: Replaces the linked evidence set. Ids are diffed against the current set: newly added ids get a FileEntityLink row (pre-upload the binaries via POST /api/core/v1/files), removed ids get their link soft-deleted. The AeroTask minimum-evidence rule applies at create time only — the QC reviewer editing a request may remove all images.
evidence_file_ids.title: Evidence File Ids

initial_evaluation_condition.description: Replaces the stored initial-evaluation condition section (custom_fields.initial_evaluation_condition). Pass null to clear it; omit to leave it unchanged. Its image_file_ids are diffed into FileEntityLink rows like evidence_file_ids.

current_condition.description: Replaces the stored current-condition section (custom_fields.current_condition). Pass null to clear it; omit to leave it unchanged. Its image_file_ids are diffed into FileEntityLink rows like evidence_file_ids.

AdminActivityInput.description:

and "add an activity to an already-created one" (``add_workorder_activity``

``estimated_duration_minutes`` stays optional here -- adding to an existing
WO has never required one -- but if given it must be a real, positive
number, never the old silent-zero default. Workorder *creation* additionally
requires every activity to carry one; see
``CreateAdminWorkorderPayload.validate_payload``.

``image_required`` (FEAT-2554) mirrors the ``custom_fields`` shape the
"Replace Cleaning Cloth" field activity already uses to require a photo

CreateAdminWorkorderPayload.description:
Payload for creating an ADMIN workorder pinned to a single technician.

An admin workorder is standalone work (no service order line) scoped to the
currently-open project: it inherits the project's ``requesting_customer`` so
the row is visible under the customer-scoped RLS policy and returned by the
project ``board-data`` query. ``assignee_resource_id`` pins the WO to one
individual so the board routes it into that member's person lane; the
resource must belong to an active project resource set of this project.

``activities`` requires at least one entry -- AeroTask's start/finish/
update flow acts on WorkorderActivity rows, not bare workorders, so an
ADMIN WO with none is inert on mobile (DISP-2379). FEAT-2554 dropped the
free-text whole-WO ``description`` in favour of the Activities section
(which now always carries real, timed activities) and caps their combined
duration at the workorder's own -- both enforced below.

``auto_carry_over`` is opt-in (DISP-3391): while the workorder is
incomplete, the hourly carry-over task keeps shifting its planned window
onto the site's current day.
CreateAdminWorkorderPayload.title: CreateAdminWorkorderPayload

ResolveCertTokenPayload.description:
Body for POST /team-requests/{id}/resolve-cert-token.

The doc-controller picks one unresolved token and tells the server what to
do with it: ``map`` it to an existing Certificate, ``create`` a fresh
Certificate then map, or ``drop`` it (strip with no new requirement).

The token is stripped from both pre-job cert answers — the
``required_certifications`` list and the free-text
``other_certification_details`` — across every site the TR spans. Matching
nothing is a 422, not a silent success.

collapsed into a single row: ``co_item_ids`` holds every contributing CO line

CoveragePublishedPayload.description:
Payload WMS sends when a roster layer is published.

project_codes is the union of every project_code with at least one
assignment in the published layer's date range — WMS doesn't diff
against the prior snapshot. Our handler is idempotent so receiving
untouched codes is harmless. The ``Literal`` on ``event`` rejects
any other event type at the API boundary, before fan-out runs.

Uses plain ``ninja.Schema`` (not the ``extra='forbid'`` REST base) on
purpose: this is an inbound webhook from an external system, so unknown
fields WMS may add later are ignored rather than 422-rejected — the
integration stays forward-compatible without a lock-step deploy.
CoveragePublishedPayload.title: CoveragePublishedPayload

TaskUpdatedPayload.description:
Payload the travel app sends when one of its travel requests changes.

Uses plain ``ninja.Schema`` (not the ``extra='forbid'`` REST base) on
purpose: this is an inbound webhook from an external system, so unknown
fields the travel app may add later are ignored rather than 422-rejected —
the integration stays forward-compatible without a lock-step deploy.

Only ``project_code`` is consumed — it identifies which project to recompute
(the recompute re-reads the Travel API by project code). ``reference`` and
``event`` are accepted for logging/observability only.
TaskUpdatedPayload.title: TaskUpdatedPayload

AiAnomalyCoreSchema.description:
The ``core.anomaly`` columns registration writes that vis.ai_anomaly lacks.

A registration spans two tables, and until this existed the response showed
only the vis half — so a caller could not tell a column it never sent from
one the service dropped, and had to query the database to find out. Covers
the taxonomy cascade, the blade context resolved from
``service_order_line_id`` + ``component_name``, and the fields that are
derived when omitted (``name``, ``rib``).
AiAnomalyCoreSchema.title: AiAnomalyCoreSchema

AiAnomalySchema.description:
Response for a vis.AiAnomaly row — every column on the table.

``deleted_at`` is deliberately omitted (soft-delete internals are never
exposed); ``core_anomaly_id`` is the ``anomaly`` FK under its API name, and
``core_anomaly`` carries the half of the registration that lives on
``core.anomaly``.
AiAnomalySchema.title: AiAnomalySchema

AiAnomalyRegisterSchema.description:
Input for POST /vis/v1/ai-anomalies — the REST twin of registerAiDefect.

Field names and semantics mirror the GraphQL ``RegisterAiDefectInput``; both
surfaces feed the same ``vis.anomalies.register_ai_defect`` service.

Exactly one identifier must be supplied, matching internal_external:
``inference_defect_id`` for INTERNAL detections (they exist in the inference
pipeline) or ``defect_uid`` for EXTERNAL ones (they do not). BOTH accepts
either. This mirrors the vis.AiAnomaly CHECK constraints.

``component_name`` is the VIS blade name used to resolve the blade context.
The six ``*_component_id`` / ``*_type_id`` / ``material_id`` fields are the
anomaly taxonomy cascade and land on ``core.anomaly``. External detections
send none of them in practice, nor a ``qr_code`` or ``segmentation``. None
of that is enforced — the importer imposes no such restriction either, and
``type_id`` / ``sub_type_id`` / ``material_id`` have always been accepted
for externals.

``name`` and ``rib`` are optional because a caller need not know them:
omitted, they are derived from the blade context — ``component_name``, or
the blade section of the ``source_object`` — matching what
``AIAnomalyImporter`` writes for a pulled defect. A supplied value wins.
AiAnomalyRegisterSchema.title: AiAnomalyRegisterSchema

AiAnomalySourceObjectSchema.description:
Input for PATCH /vis/v1/ai-anomalies/{id}/source-object.

The drone pipeline registers a defect before the portal has registered the
photo it came from, so the generic ``source_object`` pair is filled in once
that id exists.

A partial update: an omitted field is left untouched, while an explicit
``null`` clears that column. Patching one half of the pair never disturbs
the other, so the handler forwards presence rather than value.
AiAnomalySourceObjectSchema.title: AiAnomalySourceObjectSchema

CampaignWithScopeCreate.description:
Create a Campaign pre-scoped to a set of parks in one atomic call.

Replaces AeroCore's best-effort multi-call orchestration (create Campaign,
then N WorkPackages, then cleanup-on-failure). One WorkPackage is created per
``location_ids`` entry, each pinned via ``WorkPackage.site``.
CampaignWithScopeCreate.title: CampaignWithScopeCreate

WorkPackageWithScopeCreate.description:
Create work package(s) pre-scoped to selected turbines (or a park) atomically.

Productionises AeroCore's ``create-work-package-with-scope`` Track-2 shim (a
per-turbine loop with client-side cleanup-on-failure) as one transaction.

``mode``:
- ``"single"`` / ``"per-turbine"`` — one WorkPackage per ``turbine_ids`` entry,
  each pinned via ``WorkPackage.turbine``.
- ``"one-for-all"`` — a single WorkPackage covering a whole park, pinned via
  ``WorkPackage.site`` (turbines are not individually linked).
WorkPackageWithScopeCreate.title: WorkPackageWithScopeCreate

WorkPackageCampaignRow.description:

Productionises AeroCore's ``get-turbines-with-active-campaigns`` shim.

PlanningStatusesResponse.description:
Authoritative planning status catalogue, one list per entity.

Campaign, Project, ServiceOrder and WorkOrder all share the single unified
``PlanningStatus`` enum today, so the four lists are identical. The per-entity
shape is kept so the contract can diverge later without a breaking change.
